Honíble B.S.Verma, J. (Oral)
Since the controversy involved in all these writ
petitions is same, therefore, for sake of convenience, these
writ petitions are being disposed of by this common
judgment and order.
WPMS No.1867 of 2007 has been filed for quashing
the impugned order no.692/Vidhi/ni.sa.sa/2002 dated
28.11.2002 passed by respondent no.2 and orders
no.1056/A/Sa-Sahakarita/03 dated 21.3.2003 and
160/Sa.ga.a/03 dated 30.5.2003 and dated 29.6.2007
passed by the respondent no.1.
WPMS No.1868 of 2007 has been filed for quashing
the impugned order no.689/Vidhi/ni.sa.sa/2002 dated
27.11.2002 passed by respondent no.2 and orders
no.1056/A/Sa-Sahakarita/03 dated 21.3.2003 and
160/Sa.ga.a/03 dated 30.5.2003 and dated 29.6.2007
passed by the respondent no.1.
WPMS No.1869 of 2007 has been filed for quashing
the impugned order no.691/Vidhi/ni.sa.sa/2002 dated
28.11.2002 passed by respondent no.2 and orders
no.1056/A/Sa-Sahakarita/03 dated 21.3.2003 and
160/Sa.ga.a/03 dated 30.5.2003 and dated 29.6.2007
passed by the respondent no.1.
WPMS No.1870 of 2007 has been filed for quashing
the impugned order no.693 dated 28.11.2002 passed by
respondent no.2 and order no.1056 dated 21.3.2003 and

3
order no.160 dated 30.5.2003 and order no.Nil dated
29.6.2007 passed by the respondent no.1.
Learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner
has submitted that by order dated 30.5.2003 the appeals
were dismissed on the issue of limitation. Against that
order, the petitioner filed writ petitions before this Court
bearing WPMS No.819 of 2006, WPMS No.820 of 2006,
WPMS No.821 of 2006 and WPMS No.822 of 2006, which
were dismissed by this Court with the observation that
the remedy lies with the petitioner to cure the defect in
order to get the appeal heard in accordance with law.
Thereafter, the petitioner removed the defects in the
appeals but by the impugned orders respondent no.1 has
again dismissed the appeals on the ground of delay.
From the impugned orders, it transpires that
respondent no.1 has dismissed the appeals on the ground
of delay but has not given any finding on the same as to
how much delay has occurred in filing the appeals. In its
orders, respondent no.1 has also discussed merit of the
case.
According to the petitioner, there was delay of
almost 30 daysí in filing the appeals. The delay of 30 days
cannot be said to be a callous delay. Therefore, in the
interest of justice, all the writ petitions deserve to be
allowed and the impugned orders are liable to be set aside
on this ground alone.
Accordingly, all the writ petitions are allowed. Delay
in filing the appeals are condoned. Authority concerned is

4
directed to decide the appeals, on its merit, as
expeditiously as possible, after hearing all the parties
concerned.
 (B.S.Verma,J.)
 01.08.2013
